title: Propulsion is having a moment
summary: Propulsion is gaining significant attention in the space industry, as discussed by Kevin Lausten, CEO of Morpheus Space, at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference in Salt Lake City, Utah.

title: Space Angel secures $1.75m WA Government backing to advance Western Australian spaceport plans
summary: Space Angel received a $1.75 million grant from the Western Australian Government to advance plans for a spaceport. The funding was announced by Science and Innovation Minister Stephen Dawson.

title: Tendeg Launches NewTEN Steerable Compact Antenna at SmallSat
summary: Tendeg introduced NewTEN, a two-axis steerable compact antenna designed to enhance communications performance and pointing access for small spacecraft. The product was unveiled at the SmallSat event in Salt Lake City.

title: Robotics and the future of on-orbit labor
summary: SpaceNews interviews Icarus Robotics CEO Ethan Barajas at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference about the role of robotics in future on-orbit labor. The discussion highlights advancements in space robotics and their implications for space missions.

title: Spirit Electronics Adds Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology Space Grade Components to Online Store Ahead of SmallSat 2026
summary: Spirit Electronics expanded its online store to include space-grade components from Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology ahead of SmallSat 2026. This move supports the growing demand for high-reliability electronics in the space industry.

title: The Fuel for the Next Generation of Cislunar Exploration? Technology and Talent.
summary: The article discusses the future of cislunar exploration, highlighting the importance of technology and talent for upcoming missions. It reflects on the legacy of the Apollo moon landings and their long-term impact on science and national security.

title: Tory Bruno Named Honorary Chair Of World Space Week 2027
summary: Tory Bruno, President of National Security at Blue Origin, has been named Honorary Chair of World Space Week 2027. The World Space Week Association made the announcement highlighting his leadership in the space industry.

title: New Novaspace forecast: 6,500+ EO satellites to launch by 2035
summary: A forecast by Novaspace predicts over 6,500 Earth observation satellites will launch by 2035, generating $155.9 billion in manufacturing revenues. The expansion is driven by governments increasing sovereign intelligence and surveillance capabilities.

title: Elve qualifies millimeter-wave amplifiers for spaceflight
summary: Elve, a California-based startup, has qualified its 100-watt millimeter-wave Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier platform for spaceflight. The qualification was supported by U.S. Space Force Small Business Innovation Research funding.

title: What’s next for ISR in space
summary: A SpaceNews panel led by correspondent Debra Werner discusses the future of Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) in space. The discussion was recorded in May.

title: 'You just saved the video dish': Two astronauts complete spacewalk to replace ISS antenna
summary: Astronauts Anil Menon and Sophie Adenot completed a 6.5-hour spacewalk to replace an ISS antenna. The spacewalk involved installing a new Space-to-Ground antenna on the International Space Station.

title: Starbase Louisiana: SpaceX announces enormous $100 billion Starbase launch site
summary: SpaceX announced plans for a $100 billion Starbase launch site in Louisiana, featuring 10 launch pads and capable of supporting thousands of Starship launches annually.

title: The bubbling surface of doomed supergiant star Betelgeuse has been revealed like never before
summary: Astronomers have captured unprecedented images of the bubbling surface of the doomed supergiant star Betelgeuse. The new observations provide a fresh perspective on this well-studied stellar object.

title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope will reveal the universe in a way the JWST and Hubble cannot
summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is expected to capture unprecedentedly large images of the universe, surpassing the capabilities of JWST and Hubble. The images will be so vast that no existing screen can display them.

title: Sun fires powerful M6.9 solar flare and CME toward Earth — could it boost northern lights chances this week?
summary: The Sun has emitted a powerful M6.9 solar flare and a coronal mass ejection (CME) directed toward Earth, potentially enhancing the chances of seeing northern lights this week. This activity is linked to a highly active Earth-facing sunspot.

title: Astronauts make history repairing the ISS | Space photo of the day for Aug. 25, 2026
summary: ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot and NASA astronaut Anil Menon completed a historic spacewalk to repair the ISS on Aug. 18, 2026. This marks a significant milestone in ongoing maintenance and upgrades of the International Space Station.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 25, 1997: NASA launches Advanced Composition Explorer to track solar wind and so much more
summary: NASA launched the Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) satellite on Aug. 25, 1997, to study solar wind and space weather. The mission provided critical data on energetic particles in space.

title: Polish startup Ares Shield hired to protect data center satellites with high-power microwave weapons
summary: Polish startup Ares Shield has been contracted by Florida-based Lonestar Data Holdings to protect its off-Earth data centers using high-power microwave weapons, with a deal valued up to $6 million.

title: NASA satellites ace world's 1st 'lost-in-space' GPS-free navigation experiment
summary: NASA satellites have successfully demonstrated GPS-free navigation in a groundbreaking experiment, extending their mission in space. This achievement marks the world's first use of alternative navigation methods in orbit.

title: Starbase’s future production capacity ramping up
summary: Starbase's production capacity is increasing due to heightened activity at the facility. This expansion aims to support future space missions and operations.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon Heavy to launch Roman telescope, Falcon 9 to launch Starlink satellites
summary: Falcon Heavy is set to launch the Roman Space Telescope, while Falcon 9 will deploy Starlink satellites. Five orbital launches are planned from China, the U.S., and French Guiana this week.

title: NASA’s Roman telescope nears launch, reaches final integration and rehearsal milestones
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch, scheduled for August 30, after reaching final integration and rehearsal milestones.

title: LandSpace’s Zhuque-3 topples following milestone landing
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket toppled after achieving a significant milestone with a successful landing. This marks a key advancement for China's commercial space sector.

title: Ship 41 Completes Engine Testing Ahead of Flight 14
summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14. Meanwhile, Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed fit checks for its second stage and finished building the first stage engines in preparation for the Nova rocket's debut flight, which could occur as early as 2026.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, completed its second flight and achieved a successful first-stage landing. This milestone marks a significant advancement for the company in reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location off the coast of Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 lunar mission following a recent launch failure, while SpaceX's Starlink satellites are also scheduled for deployment. The week's activities highlight both Chinese and commercial space efforts.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing the development of its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also making progress on its Eclipse program. The company is promoting its next block of Alpha rockets amid these developments.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over the past five decades. The publication underscores the agency's contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3, a mission by the European Space Agency, will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to provide unprecedented views of the Sun's outer atmosphere.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3, a space mission, captured a double eclipse where the Moon crossed its field of view. This event highlights the mission's precision in observing celestial phenomena.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and digital simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is otherwise difficult to study due to the rarity and brevity of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, a deep space asteroid mission. This offers a unique opportunity to test software millions of kilometers from Earth.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking the Sun's disk, simulating an eclipse. The mission involves two satellites working together to achieve this.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with the European space industry on September 16-17. The event aims to exchange ideas, highlight capabilities, and explore opportunities.

title: White House Wants 1,000 Annual Launches and Reentries by 2030
summary: The White House has introduced a new National Space Transportation Policy aiming for 1,000 annual launches and reentries by 2030, replacing the 2013 policy. This initiative seeks to significantly expand U.S. space transportation capabilities.

title: The Aerospace Corp’s Disksat Gains Commercial Traction
summary: The Aerospace Corporation's Disksat, a novel box-less satellite design, is gaining commercial traction. This innovative configuration is proving successful in the market.

title: Exclusive: OrbitAID to Launch RPO Demo in 2027
summary: OrbitAID plans to launch a rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO) demonstration in 2027, aiming to validate the entire satellite life extension process in a single mission. Unlike previous demonstrations, this mission will integrate both far-range inspection and close-approach maneuvers.

title: Beyond Reach Labs Unveils Flarewing Deployable Solar Arrays
summary: Beyond Reach Labs has introduced a patent-pending deployable solar array system called Flarewing, designed to fold flat during launch. This technology aims to optimize solar power generation for space applications.

title: Starcloud Announces $250M Series A Extension
summary: Starcloud has raised a $250 million Series A extension, bringing its total valuation to $2.3 billion. This follows its initial $170 million Series A round in March.

title: Letara Raises ¥2.6B to Build its Hybrid Rocket Engine Tech
summary: Japanese propulsion startup Letara raised ¥2.6 billion ($16 million) in a pre-Series A funding round to develop low-cost hybrid rocket engine technology.

title: SpaceWERX Announces 2026 STRATFI Awardees
summary: SpaceWERX announced the newest awardees of the 2026 STRATFI program during the Fed Supernova conference. The Space Force revealed these recipients as part of the Strategic Funding Increase initiative.

title: Op-ed: The Technologies That Could Define the Future of Space
summary: Daniel Biedermann, a partner at NewSpace Capital, discusses the key technologies shaping the future of space tech. The op-ed highlights emerging innovations that could drive the industry forward.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its satellite production capacity and support a wider range of missions.

title: Portal Books Dedicated Falcon 9 Amid Constrained Launch Market
summary: Portal Books a dedicated Falcon 9 launch while partnering with Maverick Space Systems to sell remaining fairing capacity amid a constrained launch market.

title: Lyntris Targets Faster Delivery Timelines in Smallsat Interview With Madison Dye
summary: Lyntris, a newly formed defense tech company, aims to improve delivery timelines for small satellites. The company was created through the merger of Vitesse Systems and Accelint earlier this year.

title: Impulse Space Scales Rideshare Program to GEO With Increased Demand
summary: Impulse Space has fully booked three rideshare missions to Geostationary Orbit (GEO) through 2028 due to increased demand. The company is now considering doubling its rideshare missions to meet this growing interest.

title: Redwire to Manufacture Edge Aerospace Data Processing Units in US
summary: Redwire has partnered with Edge Aerospace to manufacture data processing units (DPUs) in the U.S. under a licensing agreement. This collaboration aims to scale Edge Aerospace's manufacturing capabilities.

title: CesiumAstro Acquires 1Aardvark, Its 3rd Defense Systems Acquisition This Year
summary: CesiumAstro acquired 1Aardvark, a Virginia-based mission software and defense systems engineering company, marking its third defense systems acquisition this year. The deal combines CesiumAstro's satellite and communications expertise with 1Aardvark's software capabilities.

title: TrustPoint Aces C-band GNSS Interference Demo for U.S. Naval Air Systems Command
summary: TrustPoint successfully demonstrated its C-band GNSS interference resistance under a contract with the U.S. Naval Air Systems Command. This marks a key milestone for its space-based positioning and navigation solutions.

title: SSC Space Execs Talk Ground Service and Lunar Mission Growth at Smallsat
summary: SSC Space executives discuss the company's ground services and lunar mission expansion at the Small Satellite Conference. The interview highlights SSC Space's offerings in these areas.

title: NanoAvionics Upgrades its Flagship MP42 Bus Line, Adding a 500kg Platform
summary: Kongsberg NanoAvionics has upgraded its MP42 satellite bus line with a new 500 kg platform, marking its largest offering to date.

title: Kepler Launches Service on its New Optical Data Relay Constellation
summary: Kepler Communications has launched service on its new optical data relay constellation for global commercial and government customers. The service became active following a SpaceX launch.

title: KSAT Rolls Out Demonstration Campaign for Hyper Hybrid RF/Optional Network
summary: KSAT has launched a demonstration campaign for its Hyperion Hyper hybrid RF/optical relay network. The campaign aims to showcase the capabilities of the next-generation Hyper network.

title: SDA Director Says Constellation’s Tranche 1 Checkouts Progressing Faster After a Slow Start
summary: The Space Development Agency reports that on-orbit checkouts for its Tranche 1 satellites, launched in July, are progressing faster than initially expected after a slow start. This marks a significant improvement in the deployment phase of the constellation.
